animatronics.name: Renfield
animatronics._sinkVolume: MEASURED, NOT YET EAR-VERIFIED — the only value on this list that has not been heard. Renfield's speakers hang off the ReSpeaker XVF3800 (a Pi 5 has no analog jack, so there is no other non-HDMI output), and that array's hardware attenuator SATURATES at wpctl 1.00: measured on the node 0.40=-23.00dB, 0.55=-15.00dB, 0.70=-9.00dB, 0.85=-4.00dB, 1.00=0.00dB, 1.30=0.00dB. So 1.00 is full hardware scale with zero digital gain, and anything above it (Orlok's 1.3) is pure PipeWire software gain that can clip. 1.00 is therefore the correct clean starting canon for a node whose amp is unknown — set the room level on the powered speakers' own knob first, and only move this number if that is not enough. It CANNOT be self-verified on this node: the XVF3800's USB descriptors declare both terminals 0x0405 Echo-canceling speakerphone, and a 0.40/0.70/1.00/1.40 playback sweep moved his own array's reading by 0.0 dB while the residual floor DROPPED 4 dB (AES gating), so his ears are structurally deaf to his own mouth. Needs a human in the room or an off-board mic.
animatronics._ip: DELIBERATELY NULL — his Pi has never been on the network, so any address here would be a guess. mDNS overlays the real IP the moment he boots (nodeDiscoveryService.overlay keeps config as the fallback and replaces ip when a node advertises _monsterbox._tcp). Until then null makes isValidHost() false, which excludes him from control fan-out and makes httpNode throw immediately instead of dialling a stranger. Measured: null fails in ~126ms (ENOTFOUND), a made-up LAN IP takes 3.1s (EHOSTUNREACH) and could hit somebody else's device, and renfield.local hangs the full 5s timeout waiting on a multicast reply. If mDNS is blocked on the night, pin him with POST /api/orchestration/nodes/manual instead of editing this file.
